title: Yuudachi
description: A narrow street in Osaka on a summer afternoon, cumulus at the far end. Hold the pointer down and the cloud edge runs up the street toward you, the sun goes out and it pours: every surface wets by what it is made of. The asphalt darkens and takes a sheen, the concrete darkens in blotches, the walls streak only where the rain can reach them, the metal and signs bead, the leaves go dark and glisten, and puddles open in the road's real hollows in the order they would fill, each one a mirror of the poles and the grey sky, rippling under the drops. Let go and the rain stops, the sun comes back down the street, and it all dries back unevenly: thin films in the sun first, the puddles last, from their shallow edges in.
intent: Techniques research piece 5, Yuudachi (the sudden summer evening shower): a material-aware wetness model on a real photograph. Wet surfaces after Sébastien Lagarde's 'Water drop' series (https://seblagarde.wordpress.com/2013/04/14/water-drop-3b-physically-based-wet-surfaces/): porous materials darken and saturate, gloss rises, puddles on flat up-facing ground, ripples per drop. Puddle placement by Priority-Flood (Barnes, Lehman & Mulla 2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.04463) on the MoGe-2 height field of the road. Japanese yuudachi: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yūdachi

sources.author: note thanun (@notethanun)
sources.note: Osaka, Pixel 6, 3072x4080 original, shipped at 1536x2040. Metric depth and normals from MoGe-2 ViT-B (Microsoft, MIT) via tools/depth/normals.py; sky matte via tools/depth/segment.py sky; people, vehicles and signs via SAM 2.1 Hiera-Tiny (Meta, Apache-2.0) prompts; materials, sunlight, rain exposure and Priority-Flood puddle fill order baked by tools/depth/bakes/yuudachi (sam.sh, bake.py). The road's sub-centimetre unevenness (below what MoGe resolves) is synthesised; its camber is MoGe's.
